title: Planetary Nebula NGC 2899
caption: Planetary nebula NGC 2899, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 2899 · constellation Vela · about 4,500 light-years away (source figure)
credit: Image: NASA, ESA, STScI; Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: Shaped a little like a moth, or like a single macaroni noodle with its ends turned up, the planetary nebula NGC 2899 stands out against a black sky. Its central band, seen edge-on, is semi-transparent in the middle. Vela, a southern constellation, is its home, approximately 4,500 light-years away.

A planetary nebula is the cast-off gas of a dying star and has nothing to do with planets. NGC 2899 has a cylindrical outflow of gas running diagonally in two directions from its center. Radiation and stellar winds from a white dwarf of nearly 40,000 degrees Fahrenheit push the gas outward, and a fragmented ring around the middle pinches the nebula like a half-eaten doughnut.

Two companion stars may also be at work near the center, interacting with each other and helping to sculpt the gas. A forest of gaseous pillars points back toward the star system that drives the radiation and winds. The colors trace glowing hydrogen and oxygen.

understand.summary: Taken with Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3. F438W and F502N are shown in blue, F555W and F656N in green, and F814W and F658N in red.
understand.eye: Narrow filters isolate the glow of particular gases, and the F814W filter records near-infrared light the eye cannot see.

explore: NASA released this picture to mark Hubble's 35 years in orbit, as one of an assortment of recent images ranging from Mars to star-forming regions and a neighboring galaxy. The telescope was carried into low Earth orbit aboard the space shuttle Discovery on April 24, 1990.
